chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), he said:
The people have acquired three things from three [individuals]: They acquired patience from Job (peace be upon him), gratitude from Noah (peace be upon him), and jealousy from the children of Jacob.
ai.seo_question: What three traits did people acquire from Job, Noah, and the children of Jacob according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) identifies Job (Ayyub) as the archetype of patience and Noah (Nuh) as the exemplar of gratitude, while attributing jealousy to the sons of Jacob. This tradition reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Uswa* (exemplary models) from the Prophets and Patriarchs, illustrating how human character traits are often derived from the moral conduct of these revered figures.
